summary: new-since must surface a snapshot-write failure as an error, never discard it — a tracker that cannot persist its baseline has no product.
reason: The snapshot write is the whole mechanism behind new-since, not incidental bookkeeping. Discarding the error makes the CLI lie in both directions: a failed first write leaves every later run reporting 'seeded snapshot, re-run later' forever, and a failed subsequent write leaves the stale baseline in place so the same items are re-reported as new on every invocation. Both look like healthy output.
